During iteration k, row k and column k of dist\n    // never change (dist[k][k] == 0), so every row i can be updated\n    // independently: the i loop is distributed over threads and the j loop\n    // is a contiguous, branch-free, vectorizable sweep.\n    //\n    // A single parallel region spans the whole k loop; the implicit barrier\n    // of each 'omp for' provides the required k -> k+1 synchronization\n    // without re-creating the thread team per iteration.\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n\n#pragma omp parallel default(none) shared(d, p, n)\n    {\n        // For each intermediate node k\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n            const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK = d + k * n;\n            const unsigned int kk = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n\n            // For each source node i (rows are independent for a fixed k)\n#pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n                const unsigned int distIK = d[i * n + k];\n                unsigned int* __restrict__ rowI = d + i * n;\n                unsigned int* __restrict__ pathI = p + i * n;\n\n                // For each destination node j\n#pragma omp simd\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                    const unsigned int distIJ = rowI[j];\n                    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                    const bool better = newDist < distIJ;\n                    rowI[j] = better ? During iteration k every row i only needs its\n    // own data plus row k as it was after iteration k-1 (row k and column k\n    // do not change during iteration k because dist[k][k] == 0). Rows are\n    // therefore partitioned statically between threads and each thread\n    // sweeps its rows with a contiguous, branch-free, vectorizable j loop.\n    //\n    // Synchronization: instead of a full barrier after every k (which costs\n    // tens of microseconds with hundreds of threads), the thread owning row\n    // k+1 publishes a snapshot of that row into a ring buffer as soon as it\n    // has updated it in iteration k. All threads wait on that single flag\n    // before starting iteration k+1, so the result is exactly what the\n    // sequential algorithm computes. Per-thread progress counters prevent a\n    // ring slot from being overwritten while a lagging thread still reads it.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n\n    constexpr size_t RING_SLOTS = 32;\n    const size_t slots = std::min(RING_SLOTS, n);\n    const size_t stride = (n + 15) & ~static_cast<size_t>(15);  // 64-byte aligned rows\n    std::vector<unsigned int> ring(slots * stride);\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ ringData = ring.data();\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> pub(new PaddedCounter[slots]);  // pub[s] == k+1 <=> slot s holds row k\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> done;                            // done[t] == steps completed by thread t\n\n#pragma omp parallel shared(done)\n    {\n        const size_t T = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_num_threads());\n        const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n\n#pragma omp single\n        done.reset(new PaddedCounter[T]);\n        // implicit barrier after single\n\n        PaddedCounter* doneArr = done.get();\n        PaddedCounter* pubArr = pub.get();\n\n        // Static contiguous row partition: rows [lo, hi) belong to thread t.\n        const size_t base = n / T;\n        const size_t rem = n % T;\n        const size_t lo = t * base + std::min(t, rem);\n        const size_t hi = lo + base + (t < rem ? 1 : 0);\n        auto owns = [lo, hi](size_t r) noexcept { return r >= lo && r < hi; };\n\n        size_t cachedMinDone = 0;  // lower bound on min_t done[t]\n\n        // Copy row r (as it is right now) into ring slot r % slots and flag it.\n        auto publish = [&](size_t r) {\n            const size_t s = r % slots;\n            if (r >= slots) {\n                // Slot s last held row r - slots; everyone must have finished step r - slots.\n                const size_t need = r - slots + 1;\n                while (cachedMinDone < need) {\n                    size_t m = std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max();\n                    for (size_t u = 0; u < T; ++u) {\n                        m = std::min(m, doneArr[u].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire));\n                    }\n                    cachedMinDone = m;\n                    if (m < need) spinPause();\n                }\n            }\n            std::memcpy(ringData + s * stride, d + r * n, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n            pubArr[s].v.store(r + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n        };\n\n        // Relax all (i, j) through intermediate k using the published row k.\n        auto updateRow = [&](size_t i, size_t k, const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK) {\n            const unsigned int distIK = d[i * n + k];\n            const unsigned int kk = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ rowI = d + i * n;\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ pathI = p + i * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = rowI[j];\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool better = newDist < distIJ;\n                rowI[j] = better ? newDist : distIJ;\n                pathI[j] = better ? kk : pathI[j];\n            }\n        };\n\n        if (owns(0)) publish(0);\n\n        if (lo < hi) {\n            // For each intermediate node k\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                const size_t s = k % slots;\n                while (pubArr[s].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != k + 1) spinPause();\n                const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK = ringData + s * stride;\n\n                // Update the row needed by everybody next (row k+1) first and\n                // publish it immediately to keep the pipeline moving.\n                const size_t next = k + 1;\n                const bool ownsNext = next < n && owns(next);\n                if (ownsNext) {\n                    updateRow(next, k, rowK);\n                    publish(next);\n                }\n\n                // For each remaining source node i owned by this thread\n                for (size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i) {\n                    if (ownsNext && i == next) continue;\n                    updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n                }\n\n                doneArr[t].v.store(k + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n            }\n        } else {\n            // No rows for this thread (more threads than nodes): never blocks anyone.\n            doneArr[t].v.store(n, std::memory_order_release);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s.replace(old,new)\ns=s.replace('#include <algorithm>\\n','#include <algorithm>\\n#include <atomic>\\n')\ns=s.replace('#include <cstring>\\n','#include <cstring>\\n#include <limits>\\n#include <memory>\\n')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nhead -15 floydwarshall.cpp","description":"Replace kernel with pipelined point-to-point synchronized version"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1270,"cache_read_input_tokens":19856,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1270},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"29a6b8b2-e6cb-4c41-b054-2ba854734a5e","uuid":"cfe0d408-809f-46f6-8191-fe6a82dca8d5","timestamp":"2026-10-11T11:20:46.127Z","request_id":"req_011CfvMiY26fQGpBvcKPqMZp"}

Applying step k to row i only needs row i itself\n    // (including dist[i][k]) plus row k as it was after step k-1 (row k and\n    // column k do not change during step k because dist[k][k] == 0). The\n    // result is identical to the sequential algorithm as long as every row\n    // receives the steps k = 0 .. n-1 in increasing order and step k reads\n    // the \"after step k-1\" snapshot of row k.\n    //\n    // Rows are partitioned statically into one contiguous block per thread\n    // and each thread sweeps its rows with a contiguous, branch-free,\n    // vectorizable j loop.\n    //\n    // Synchronization is point-to-point instead of a barrier per step: the\n    // owner of row k publishes its \"after step k-1\" snapshot into a ring\n    // buffer and everybody waits only on that one flag. Inside its own block\n    // [lo, hi) a thread needs nothing from other threads for steps lo..hi-1,\n    // so it runs ahead and publishes rows lo+1..hi-1 as early as possible\n    // (a few row updates each) and backfills the remaining updates of its\n    // block afterwards. This keeps the per-step critical path at roughly one\n    // row update instead of a full per-thread step plus barrier latency.\n    //\n    // Per-thread progress counters prevent a ring slot from being overwritten\n    // while a lagging thread still reads it (and bound how far ahead a thread\n    // may run).\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n\n    constexpr size_t RING_SLOTS = 64;\n    const size_t slots = std::min(RING_SLOTS, n);\n    const size_t stride = (n + 15) & ~static_cast<size_t>(15);  // 64-byte row pitch\n    std::vector<unsigned int> ring(slots * stride + 16);\n    // Align the ring rows to cache lines.\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ ringData = reinterpret_cast<unsigned int*>(\n        (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(ring.data()) + 63) & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(63));\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> pub(new PaddedCounter[slots]);  // pub[s] == k+1 <=> slot s holds row k\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> done;                            // done[t] == steps completed by thread t\n    PaddedCounter sharedMinDone;                                      // cached lower bound of min_t done[t]\n\n#pragma omp parallel shared(done)\n    {\n        const size_t T = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_num_threads());\n        const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n\n#pragma omp single\n        done.reset(new PaddedCounter[T]);\n        // implicit barrier after single\n\n        PaddedCounter* doneArr = done.get();\n        PaddedCounter* pubArr = pub.get();\n\n        // Static contiguous row partition: rows [lo, hi) belong to thread t.\n        const size_t base = n / T;\n        const size_t rem = n % T;\n        const size_t lo = t * base + std::min(t, rem);\n        const size_t hi = lo + base + (t < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        // Snapshot of row k (\"after step k-1\") lives in ring slot k % slots.\n        auto ringRow = [&](size_t k) noexcept -> const unsigned int* {\n            return ringData + (k % slots) * stride;\n        };\n\n        // Block until row k has been published, then prefetch it: the row\n        // sits in the publisher's cache, so issue all line fetches at once.\n        auto acquireRow = [&](size_t k) -> const unsigned int* {\n            PaddedCounter& flag = pubArr[k % slots];\n            Backoff backoff;\n            while (flag.v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != k + 1) backoff.wait();\n            const unsigned int* rowK = ringRow(k);\n            for (size_t off = 0; off < n; off += 16) __builtin_prefetch(rowK + off, 0, 3);\n            return rowK;\n        };\n\n        // Copy row r (as it is right now) into ring slot r % slots and flag it.\n        auto publish = [&](size_t r) {\n            const size_t s = r % slots;\n            if (r >= slots) {\n                // Slot s last held row r - slots; everyone must have finished\n                // step r - slots. The scan over all threads is expensive, so\n                // its result is shared and only refreshed when insufficient.\n                const size_t need = r - slots + 1;\n                Backoff backoff;\n                while (sharedMinDone.v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) < need) {\n                    size_t m = std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max();\n                    for (size_t u = 0; u < T; ++u) {\n                        m = std::min(m, doneArr[u].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire));\n                    }\n                    size_t cur = sharedMinDone.v.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);\n                    while (cur < m && !sharedMinDone.v.compare_exchange_weak(\n                               cur, m, std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {\n                    }\n                    if (m < need) backoff.wait();\n                }\n            }\n            std::memcpy(ringData + s * stride, d + r * n, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n            pubArr[s].v.store(r + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n        };\n\n        // Apply step k to row i using the published snapshot of row k.\n        auto updateRow = [&](size_t i, size_t k, const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK) {\n            const unsigned int distIK = d[i * n + k];\n            const unsigned int kk = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ rowI = d + i * n;\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ pathI = p + i * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = rowI[j];\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool better = newDist < distIJ;\n                rowI[j] = better ? newDist : distIJ;\n                pathI[j] = better ? kk : pathI[j];\n            }\n        };\n\n        if (lo >= hi) {\n            // No rows for this thread (more threads than nodes): never blocks anyone.\n            doneArr[t].v.store(n, std::memory_order_release);\n        } else {\n            if (lo == 0) publish(0);\n\n            // Phase A: steps k < lo, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < lo; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int* rowK = acquireRow(k);\n                const bool publishLo = (k + 1 == lo);\n                if (publishLo) {\n                    // Row lo is needed by everybody next: update and publish it first.\n                    updateRow(lo, k, rowK);\n                    publish(lo);\n                }\n                for (size_t i = lo + (publishLo ? 1 : 0); i < hi; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n                doneArr[t].v.store(k + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n            }\n\n            // Phase B: steps lo <= k < hi, all required rows are our own.\n            // Invariants: a published row i has received steps [0, max(i, kDone));\n            // an unpublished row has received steps [0, kDone).\n            size_t kDone = lo;        // steps completed on all rows of the block\n            size_t nextPub = lo + 1;  // next row of the block to publish\n            while (kDone < hi) {\n                if (nextPub < hi && nextPub < kDone + slots) {\n                    // Run ahead: bring row nextPub to \"after step nextPub-1\" and publish it.\n                    for (size_t k = kDone; k < nextPub; ++k) updateRow(nextPub, k, ringRow(k));\n                    publish(nextPub);\n                    ++nextPub;\n                } else {\n                    // Backfill step kDone on the rows that have not received it yet:\n                    // published rows i <= kDone and all unpublished rows.\n                    const size_t k = kDone;\n                    const unsigned int* rowK = ringRow(k);\n                    for (size_t i = lo; i <= k; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n                    for (size_t i = nextPub; i < hi; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n                    ++kDone;\n                    doneArr[t].v.store(kDone, std::memory_order_release);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Phase C: steps k >= hi, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = hi; k < n; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int* rowK = acquireRow(k);\n                for (size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n                doneArr[t].v.store(k + 1, std::memory_order_release);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]\ns=s.replace('#include <cstring>\\n','#include <cstdint>\\n#include <cstring>\\n')\n# parallel path init: original net effect is path[i*n+j] = i for all i, j\nold_init=s[s.index('void initializePathMatrix('):s.index('namespace {')]\nnew_init='''void initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // The original loop nest writes every element path[idx2(j, i, n)] with\n    // value i (each off-diagonal element twice, both times with the same\n    // value), so each row i of the (i, j) matrix is filled with i. Write every\n    // element exactly once, with rows distributed over threads.\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        const unsigned int v = static_cast<unsigned int>(i);\n        unsigned int* row = p + i * numNodes;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n            row[j] = v;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s.replace(old_init,new_init)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncd /tmp/fw_omp && make 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error\"; for n in 512 1024; do for t in 1 3 16 64 128 256; do printf \"n=%d t=%d \" $n $t; OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t ./floydwarshall -n $n -v -r > out_${n}_$t.txt; grep -E \"Perf|FAILED\" out_${n}_$t.txt | tr '\\n' ' '; cmp -s <(grep -v -E \"time|Perf\" out_${n}_$t.txt) <(grep -v -E \"time|Perf\" /tmp/fw_base/out1024.txt) && echo \"identical to baseline\" || echo; done; done","description":"Rewrite kernel with run-ahead block publishing, parallel path init, rebuild and verify"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2084,"cache_read_input_tokens":59148,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2084},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"29a6b8b2-e6cb-4c41-b054-2ba854734a5e","uuid":"47d80331-34f5-4e5f-8a2d-dff33a47aea2","timestamp":"2026-10-11T11:30:43.036Z","request_id":"req_011CfvNN2iHgnvFDPwnjNzqB"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfvNrG4k88yD6zWq38vTg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014WrVu8cDCb9sNJbGV72dQQ","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd floydwarshall && python3 - <<'EOF'\np='floydwarshall.cpp'\ns=open(p).read()\nstart=s.index('void floydWarshall(')\nend=s.index('bool validateResult(')\nnew=r'''void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized with OpenMP.\n    //\n    // Memory layout: idx2(j, i, n) == i * n + j, so row i of the (i, j)\n    // matrix is contiguous. Applying step k to row i only needs row i itself\n    // (including dist[i][k]) plus row k as it was after step k-1 (row k and\n    // column k do not change during step k because dist[k][k] == 0). The\n    // result is identical to the sequential algorithm as long as every row\n    // receives the steps k = 0 .. n-1 in increasing order and step k reads\n    // the \"after step k-1\" snapshot of row k.\n    //\n    // Rows are partitioned statically into one contiguous block per thread\n    // and each thread sweeps its rows with a contiguous, branch-free,\n    // vectorizable j loop.\n    //\n    // Synchronization is point-to-point instead of a barrier per step: the\n    // owner of row k publishes its \"after step k-1\" snapshot into a\n    // write-once snapshot buffer (one slot per row, so a publish never has\n    // to invalidate lines cached by other readers) and everybody waits only\n    // on that row's flag. Inside its own block [lo, hi) a thread needs\n    // nothing from other threads for steps lo..hi-1, so it runs ahead and\n    // publishes rows lo+1..hi-1 as early as possible (a few row updates\n    // each) and backfills the remaining updates of its block afterwards.\n    // This keeps the per-step critical path at roughly one row update\n    // instead of a full per-thread step plus barrier latency.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n\n    // Snapshot buffer: row k (\"after step k-1\") is stored at snap + k * stride.\n    // Allocated uninitialized and first-touched by the publishing thread.\n    const size_t stride = (n + 15) & ~static_cast<size_t>(15);  // 64-byte row pitch\n    std::unique_ptr<unsigned int[]> snapStorage(new unsigned int[n * stride + 16]);\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ snap = reinterpret_cast<unsigned int*>(\n        (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(snapStorage.get()) + 63) & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(63));\n    // pub[k] == 1 once row k has been published.\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> pubStorage(new PaddedCounter[n]);\n    PaddedCounter* pubArr = pubStorage.get();\n\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const size_t T = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_num_threads());\n        const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n\n        // Static contiguous row partition: rows [lo, hi) belong to thread t.\n        const size_t base = n / T;\n        const size_t rem = n % T;\n        const size_t lo = t * base + std::min(t, rem);\n        const size_t hi = lo + base + (t < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        // First-touch the snapshot slots this thread will publish, so the\n        // page faults happen in parallel and off the critical path.\n        if (lo < hi) std::memset(snap + lo * stride, 0, (hi - lo) * stride * sizeof(unsigned int));\n\n        auto snapRow = [&](size_t k) noexcept -> const unsigned int* {\n            return snap + k * stride;\n        };\n\n        // Block until row k has been published, then prefetch it: the row\n        // sits in the publisher's cache, so issue all line fetches at once.\n        auto acquireRow = [&](size_t k) -> const unsigned int* {\n            PaddedCounter& flag = pubArr[k];\n            Backoff backoff;\n            while (flag.v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0) backoff.wait();\n            const unsigned int* rowK = snapRow(k);\n            for (size_t off = 0; off < n; off += 16) __builtin_prefetch(rowK + off, 0, 3);\n            return rowK;\n        };\n\n        // Copy row r (as it is right now) into its snapshot slot and flag it.\n        auto publish = [&](size_t r) {\n            std::memcpy(snap + r * stride, d + r * n, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n            pubArr[r].v.store(1, std::memory_order_release);\n        };\n\n        // Apply step k to row i using the published snapshot of row k.\n        auto updateRow = [&](size_t i, size_t k, const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK) {\n            const unsigned int distIK = d[i * n + k];\n            const unsigned int kk = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ rowI = d + i * n;\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ pathI = p + i * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = rowI[j];\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool better = newDist < distIJ;\n                rowI[j] = better ? newDist : distIJ;\n                pathI[j] = better ? kk : pathI[j];\n            }\n        };\n\n        if (lo < hi) {\n            if (lo == 0) publish(0);\n\n            // Phase A: steps k < lo, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < lo; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int* rowK = acquireRow(k);\n                const bool publishLo = (k + 1 == lo);\n                if (publishLo) {\n                    // Row lo is needed by everybody next: update and publish it first.\n                    updateRow(lo, k, rowK);\n                    publish(lo);\n                }\n                for (size_t i = lo + (publishLo ? 1 : 0); i < hi; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n            }\n\n            // Phase B: steps lo <= k < hi, all required rows are our own.\n            // Run ahead: row r only needs steps lo..r-1, whose snapshots are\n            // ours, so publish rows lo+1..hi-1 right away (row r = lo + m\n            // costs m updates), then backfill the remaining updates. Every\n            // row still receives its steps in increasing order: row r gets\n            // steps lo..r-1 here and steps r..hi-1 in the backfill below.\n            for (size_t r = lo + 1; r < hi; ++r) {\n                for (size_t k = lo; k < r; ++k) updateRow(r, k, snapRow(k));\n                publish(r);\n            }\n            for (size_t k = lo; k < hi; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int* rowK = snapRow(k);\n                for (size_t i = lo; i <= k; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n            }\n\n            // Phase C: steps k >= hi, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = hi; k < n; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int* rowK = acquireRow(k);\n                for (size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i) updateRow(i, k, rowK);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s[:start]+new+s[end:]\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ngrep -n \"limits\\|sched\\|atomic\" floydwarshall.cpp | head; cd /tmp/fw_omp && make 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error\"; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01ECokMnvhopBHTGpyxosEoZ","type":"tool_result","content":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized with OpenMP.\n    //\n    // Memory layout: idx2(j, i, n) == i * n + j, so row i of the (i, j)\n    // matrix is contiguous. Applying step k to row i only needs row i itself\n    // (including dist[i][k]) plus row k as it was after step k-1 (row k and\n    // column k do not change during step k because dist[k][k] == 0). The\n    // result is identical to the sequential algorithm as long as every row\n    // receives the steps k = 0 .. n-1 in increasing order and step k reads\n    // the \"after step k-1\" snapshot of row k.\n    //\n    // Rows are partitioned statically into one contiguous block per thread\n    // and each thread sweeps its rows with a contiguous, branch-free,\n    // vectorizable j loop.\n    //\n    // Synchronization is point-to-point instead of a barrier per step: the\n    // owner of row k publishes its \"after step k-1\" snapshot into a\n    // write-once snapshot buffer (one slot per row, so a publish never has\n    // to invalidate lines cached by other readers) and everybody waits only\n    // on that row's flag. Inside its own block [lo, hi) a thread needs\n    // nothing from other threads for steps lo..hi-1, so it runs ahead and\n    // publishes rows lo+1..hi-1 as early as possible (a few row updates\n    // each) and backfills the remaining updates of its block afterwards.\n    // This keeps the per-step critical path at roughly one row update\n    // instead of a full per-thread step plus barrier latency.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ p = path.data();\n\n    // Snapshot buffer: row k (\"after step k-1\") is stored at snap + k * stride.\n    // Allocated uninitialized and first-touched by the publishing thread.\n    const size_t stride = (n + 15) & ~static_cast<size_t>(15);  // 64-byte row pitch\n    std::unique_ptr<unsigned int[]> snapStorage(new unsigned int[n * stride + 16]);\n    unsigned int* __restrict__ snap = reinterpret_cast<unsigned int*>(\n        (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(snapStorage.get()) + 63) & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(63));\n    // pub[k] == 1 once row k has been published.\n    std::unique_ptr<PaddedCounter[]> pubStorage(new PaddedCounter[n]);\n    PaddedCounter* pubArr = pubStorage.get();\n\n    // Give every thread at least a few rows: with fewer rows per thread the\n    // per-step synchronization dominates and extra threads only slow it down.\n    const int numThreads = static_cast<int>(\n        std::max<size_t>(1, std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads()), n / 8)));\n\n#pragma omp parallel num_threads(numThreads)\n    {\n        const size_t T = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_num_threads());\n        const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_thread_num());\n\n        // Bind threads unless the user already chose a binding policy.\n        if (T > 1 && omp_get_proc_bind() == omp_proc_bind_false) pinThread(t);\n\n        // Static contiguous row partition: rows [lo, hi) belong to thread t.\n        const size_t base = n / T;\n        const size_t rem = n % T;\n        const size_t lo = t * base + std::min(t, rem);\n        const size_t hi = lo + base + (t < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        // First-touch the snapshot slots this thread will publish, so the\n        // page faults happen in parallel and off the critical path.\n        if (lo < hi) std::memset(snap + lo * stride, 0, (hi - lo) * stride * sizeof(unsigned int));\n\n        auto snapRow = [&](size_t k) noexcept -> const unsigned int* {\n            return snap + k * stride;\n        };\n\n        auto prefetchRow = [&](size_t k) noexcept {\n            const unsigned int* rowK = snapRow(k);\n            for (size_t off = 0; off < n; off += 16) __builtin_prefetch(rowK + off, 0, 3);\n        };\n\n        // Copy row r (as it is right now) into its snapshot slot and flag it.\n        // The snapshot is written with streaming stores: hundreds of readers\n        // then pull it from memory through all channels instead of hammering\n        // the publisher's cache / its CCD link with a single-source broadcast.\n        auto publish = [&](size_t r) {\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ dst = snap + r * stride;\n            const unsigned int* __restrict__ src = d + r * n;\n            size_t j = 0;\n#if defined(__AVX2__)\n            for (; j + 8 <= n; j += 8) {\n                _mm256_stream_si256(reinterpret_cast<__m256i*>(dst + j),\n                                    _mm256_loadu_si256(reinterpret_cast<const __m256i*>(src + j)));\n            }\n#elif defined(__SSE2__)\n            for (; j + 4 <= n; j += 4) {\n                _mm_stream_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(dst + j),\n                                 _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(src + j)));\n            }\n#endif\n            for (; j < n; ++j) dst[j] = src[j];\n#if defined(__SSE2__)\n            _mm_sfence();  // streaming stores are weakly ordered: drain before the flag\n#endif\n            pubArr[r].v.store(1, std::memory_order_release);\n        };\n\n        // Apply step k to row i using the published snapshot of row k.\n        auto updateRow = [&](size_t i, size_t k, const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowK) {\n            const unsigned int distIK = d[i * n + k];\n            const unsigned int kk = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ rowI = d + i * n;\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ pathI = p + i * n;\n#pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = rowI[j];\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                const bool better = newDist < distIJ;\n                rowI[j] = better ? newDist : distIJ;\n                pathI[j] = better ? kk : pathI[j];\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Steps whose rows come from other threads are consumed in chunks of\n        // consecutive already-published rows [k, k + K): each own row then\n        // receives the K steps (in increasing order) while it stays in L1,\n        // instead of streaming the whole block through the cache once per\n        // step. Only row k is ever waited for; K adapts to what is available.\n        // kMax keeps the K snapshot rows within about 256 KB of L2.\n        const size_t kMax = std::max<size_t>(1, std::min<size_t>(64, (256u * 1024u) / (n * sizeof(unsigned int))));\n\n        // Wait for row k, then return the number of consecutively published\n        // rows starting at k, capped at limit. Prefetches the flags and the\n        // first rows of the chunk so the fetches overlap with computation.\n        auto acquireChunk = [&](size_t k, size_t limit) -> size_t {\n            for (size_t q = 1; q < limit; ++q) __builtin_prefetch(&pubArr[k + q], 0, 3);\n            Backoff backoff;\n            while (pubArr[k].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0) backoff.wait();\n            size_t K = 1;\n            while (K < limit && pubArr[k + K].v.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0) ++K;\n            prefetchRow(k);\n            if (K > 1) prefetchRow(k + 1);\n            return K;\n        };\n\n        // Apply steps [k, k + K) to all own rows (row-major), publishing row\n        // lo as soon as it has reached the state \"after step lo - 1\".\n        auto consumeChunk = [&](size_t k, size_t K) {\n            for (size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i) {\n                for (size_t q = 0; q < K; ++q) updateRow(i, k + q, snapRow(k + q));\n                if (i == lo && k + K == lo) publish(lo);  // row lo is needed by everybody next\n            }\n        };\n\n        if (lo < hi) {\n            if (lo == 0) publish(0);\n\n            // Phase A: steps k < lo, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < lo;) {\n                const size_t K = acquireChunk(k, std::min(kMax, lo - k));\n                consumeChunk(k, K);\n                k += K;\n            }\n\n            // Phase B: steps lo <= k < hi, all required rows are our own.\n            // Run ahead: row r only needs steps lo..r-1, whose snapshots are\n            // ours, so publish rows lo+1..hi-1 right away (row r = lo + m\n            // costs m updates), then backfill the remaining updates. Every\n            // row still receives its steps in increasing order: row r gets\n            // steps lo..r-1 here and steps r..hi-1 in the backfill below.\n            for (size_t r = lo + 1; r < hi; ++r) {\n                for (size_t k = lo; k < r; ++k) updateRow(r, k, snapRow(k));\n                publish(r);\n            }\n            for (size_t i = lo; i < hi; ++i) {\n                for (size_t k = i; k < hi; ++k) updateRow(i, k, snapRow(k));\n            }\n\n            // Phase C: steps k >= hi, row k comes from another thread.\n            for (size_t k = hi; k < n;) {\n                const size_t K = acquireChunk(k, std::min(kMax, n - k));\n                consumeChunk(k, K);\n                k += K;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfvPZAcUXXXizzLs7fZp6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The Floyd-Warshall benchmark is now OpenMP-parallel, produces output bit-identical to the original for every size and thread count I tested, and runs up to several hundred times faster.\n\n**What changed** (only `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` and `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`):\n\n- **CMake** finds OpenMP as a required package and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. The executable name is unchanged.\n- **Kernel decomposition.** Rows are split into one contiguous block per thread. Step k on a row needs only that row plus a snapshot of row k as it was after step k-1, so each row receives steps in increasing k order, which is exactly what makes the result identical to the sequential algorithm, including the path matrix tie-breaking.\n- **No per-step barrier.** The owner of row k publishes its snapshot into a write-once buffer and sets a flag. Everyone else waits only on that flag. Inside its own block a thread needs nothing from others, so it publishes its remaining rows early and backfills afterwards. This keeps the per-step critical path at about one row update.\n- **Broadcast fix.** Snapshots are written with streaming stores so hundreds of readers pull the row through the memory channels instead of saturating one core's cache link. Profiling showed that single-source broadcast was costing 10-16K cycles per step.\n- **Cache blocking.** Consumers apply up to 64 consecutive already-published steps to each row while it sits in L1, which fixed DRAM thrashing for large n with few threads.\n- **Thread placement.** Threads are pinned to distinct CPUs unless the user set `OMP_PROC_BIND` or `OMP_PLACES`, and the thread count is capped at n/8 so tiny problems are not drowned in sync overhead.\n- **Inner loop** is branch-free and auto-vectorized with AVX2. The untimed path-matrix init is also parallel.\n\n**Measured throughput** on this 2-socket, 128-core EPYC box with the thread count unset (original: 0.88 GOPS at n=1024):\n\n| n | GOPS (default threads) |\n|---|---|\n| 512 | 45-67 |\n| 1024 | 107-153 |\n| 2048 | 230-300 |\n| 4096 | 320-340 |\n\n**Verification.** Hash output and validation match the original binary for n in {1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 17, 64, 100, 257, 512, 513, 1024} at 1, 3, 7, 16, 64, 128, and 256 threads, with both the AVX2 and the SSE2 fallback build. One caveat: the machine had other users' load during measurement, so the n=512 numbers vary by about 2x from run to run because the timer has millisecond resolution and the run takes 2-5 ms."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":625,"cache_read_input_tokens":135552,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":625},"output_tokens":744,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"29a6b8b2-e6cb-4c41-b054-2ba854734a5e","uuid":"78a9b0d6-eb09-4998-82f0-9f59e5969130","timestamp":"2026-10-11T11:42:54.302Z","request_id":"req_011CfvPZA1GUBAh4zBN12RNe"}
